name: Christian Texts
description: The sacred scriptures and writings that form the foundation of Christian faith and theology. From the canonical Bible to the writings of the early Church Fathers, these texts have shaped Christian thought and practice for two millennia.
longDescription:
The sacred scriptures and writings that form the foundation of Christian faith and theology. From the canonical Bible to the writings of the early Church Fathers, these texts have shaped Christian thought and practice for two millennia.

The central sacred text of Christianity, comprising the Old and New Testaments, considered divinely inspired scripture revealing God's relationship with humanity.

The Hebrew scriptures inherited from Judaism. Chronicles creation, the covenant with Israel, and prophecies of the coming Messiah.

Major sections: Pentateuch, Historical Books, Wisdom Literature, Prophets

The distinctly Christian scriptures centered on the life, teachings, death, and resurrection of Jesus Christ. Includes the Gospels, Acts, Epistles, and Revelation.

Major sections: Four Gospels, Acts of the Apostles, Pauline Epistles, General Epistles, Revelation

Additional books included in Catholic and Orthodox Bibles but not in Protestant canons. Include Tobit, Judith, Wisdom, Sirach, Baruch, and Maccabees.

Status: Canonical in Catholic/Orthodox traditions

Writings from the generation immediately following the apostles (late 1st to mid-2nd century). Includes the Didache, Clement's letters, and Ignatius's epistles.

Influential early Christian theologians and teachers who shaped doctrine. Includes Irenaeus, Tertullian, Origen, Augustine, Jerome, and the Cappadocian Fathers.

Official statements and creeds from the seven ecumenical councils that defined Christian orthodoxy. Include the Nicene Creed (325 CE) and Chalcedonian Definition (451 CE).

The formal orders of worship and prayer used in Christian services. Includes the Divine Liturgy, the Roman Missal, and the Book of Common Prayer.

Collections of psalms, hymns, prayers, and readings for the Liturgy of the Hours. The 150 Psalms form the heart of Christian contemplative tradition.

Hagiographies documenting the lives, miracles, and martyrdoms of Christian saints. These texts inspire faith and preserve sacred memory.
